items.stem: Why should a private database subnet not have a route to an internet gateway?

options.text: It exposes the database directly to the internet, widening the attack surface
options.rationale: Correct: private tiers should not be directly internet-reachable.
The concern is exposure, not speed.
Databases use IP addressing like any host.

options.text: It would disable the security groups
options.rationale: A route does not disable security groups.

items.explanation: Correct: private tiers should not be directly internet-reachable.

items.stem: Which TWO are good practices when planning cloud IP addressing? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Choose CIDR ranges that do not overlap on-premises networks
options.rationale: Correct: overlaps break routing to on-premises.

options.text: Leave room to add subnets as the environment grows
options.rationale: Correct: planning headroom avoids re-addressing later.

options.text: Reuse the same CIDR in every network for simplicity
options.rationale: Identical ranges collide when networks connect.

options.text: Assign one giant subnet with no segmentation
options.rationale: Flat networks remove isolation between tiers.

items.stem: A private subnet's instances need to download patches but must not accept inbound internet traffic. What fits?

options.text: A NAT gateway for outbound-only internet access
options.rationale: Correct: NAT allows outbound connections without inbound exposure.

options.text: An internet gateway with a public IP on each instance
options.rationale: That exposes instances to inbound traffic.
With no route the patches cannot be fetched.

options.text: A VPN only to another cloud
options.rationale: A VPN to another cloud does not reach public patch servers.

items.explanation: Correct: NAT allows outbound connections without inbound exposure.
